cells.tense: Right now what's fair has a shape you can see from far enough back.
cells.ask: Take one stretch that's finished with you and name what it gave you — including the part you'd have traded back.
cells.core:
You know what's fair the way you know a pattern — by the shape it makes, not by anybody's rule. Somebody gets more credit than they earned and you feel the wrongness of it before you've found the reasons. That's a compass, and it's working. It arrives stripped of the story, which is why you can be certain and still unable to explain, and why people sometimes take your certainty as coldness.

There's a stretch of your life that's done with you now. Gather what it actually gave you — not what you'd have chosen, not what you'd have traded it for. Put it in writing, or say it plainly to somebody who was there to see it. What a finished thing handed over is usually the part nobody has ever asked you about, and the part still doing work in you.
cells.sheetLine: What's fair shows up as a shape before it shows up as words.
cells.verb: knowing what's right and what's owed
cells.place: a clear room with the furniture taken out of it

cells.tense: You will be reckoning against a bill nobody has handed you yet.
cells.act: give a concrete piece of help and finish it
cells.ask: Pick one person you've been meaning to help. Do one specific thing for them today and take it all the way to done.
cells.core:
Where you know what's owed, the reckoning arrives before the facts do. You're settling accounts that haven't been opened, costing out a future nobody has spent yet, and the arithmetic won't come out because the numbers aren't in. From a distance it looks like clear eyes. Up close it's a court keeping its own hours, and it costs you people who got no summons.

Fair doesn't come from getting there first. Give someone one concrete hand today — the errand, the ride, the form they can't face — and take it all the way to the end. Finishing is the part that usually gets skipped. When it's done, stop. The tally will still be there, and it will be smaller than it looks from here.

cells.tense: You stopped calling it unfair some time back, and the case is still open.
cells.act: walk the route with someone who is lost on it
cells.ask: Take someone who's stuck on a stretch you once got out of. Walk them through your route once, plainly, step by step.
cells.core:
You can still spot what isn't fair. Spotting it and saying it have come apart, and the saying is the half that went quiet. The wrongness just sits there now, and being able to call it has become a private skill nobody else gets the use of. You didn't decide to stop. You've been behind a door that closed, and nobody on the near side knows what you clocked before you went still.

You found a way out of something once. Name one person tangled in that same stretch and talk them the way out in plain words: what you did, in order, step and step. Tell it one time through. Being told the route is how the route returns — not by rehearsing it alone, but by handing it to somebody still on the path.

cells.tense: Nothing in the room looks like weighing, and the scale is already tipped.
cells.act: list the pulls on you and mark which are yours
cells.ask: Keep a page this week of everything pulling at you, and mark the lines that are actually yours and leave the rest unmarked.
cells.core:
You keep things fair among the people close to you, quietly, and if anyone asked you'd say you're only watching. The reading of what's owed lands before the reasoning does — you catch the shape of a situation and move, and the account of why you moved shows up afterward dressed as thought. The ones near you have been living on this. You've been calling it staying neutral.

Make a page of what's pulling at you this week, one thing to a line. Go back and mark only the ones that belong to you — your promise, your name signed to it — and leave the others standing there unmarked. The borrowed ones give themselves away by how loudly they argue. Nothing gets dropped today. The page just tells the truth about whose load each line is.
